correctness.rationale: For fixed m, count pairs ab <= X with ab congruent to r modulo m by the divisor hyperbola split. For a <= sqrt(X), the count in b is X gcd(a,m)/(am) + O(1) if gcd(a,m) divides r, and zero otherwise. Doubling this count and subtracting the common square costs O(X) outside the main term. The harmonic sum of the periodic function gcd(a,m) times the divisibility indicator has leading coefficient its mean. The resulting X log X weight is m^(-2) times the sum of gcd(a,m) over a modulo m for which gcd(a,m) divides r. CRT factors this mean. For p^a the terms with valuation k<a each contribute a total p^(a-1)(p-1) when k <= v_p(r), and the zero class contributes p^a if p^a divides r. This proves precisely the two frozen weights and handles the infinite-limit step without a tail interchange. In the finite optimization, conditioning on the first vertex ensures the end constraint is checked, and the last-selected/not-selected recurrence exhausts the remaining path choices; for m=1 the cyclic rule forbids the sole vertex. Independent exact calculation through 90 confirms no strict gain for m<90 and optimum 2040/2700 at 90, with the stated swap (63-24-24) improving 2025 to 2040. The finite reproduction and analytic asymptotic are separate checks.
